claim: The archicortical hippocampus differs in its folding patterns across individuals, like neocortical structures.
source: Like neocortical structures, the archicortical hippocampus differs in its folding patterns across individuals.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a foundational premise for the work.

claim: Most neurological or psychiatric diseases with widespread effects on the brain show strong and early impact on the hippocampus.
source: Most neurological or psychiatric diseases with widespread effects on the brain show strong and early impact on the hippocampus (e.g. Thom, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Thom, 2014.

claim: The hippocampus is critical in the fast formation of episodic and spatial memories.
source: This highly plastic grey matter (GM) structure is also critical in the fast formation of episodic and spatial memories (e.g. O'Keefe and Nadel, 1978).
evidence: Supported by citation to O'Keefe and Nadel, 1978.

claim: The hippocampus is typically modelled as a subcortical volume in current neuroimaging analyses.
source: In current neuroimaging analyses the hippocampus is typically modelled as a subcortical volume, but it is actually made up of a folded archicortical mantle, or 'ribbon' (Duvernoy, 1998).
evidence: Stated as current practice with citation to Duvernoy, 1998 for the ribbon structure.

claim: The hippocampus is actually made up of a folded archicortical mantle, or 'ribbon'.
source: In current neuroimaging analyses the hippocampus is typically modelled as a subcortical volume, but it is actually made up of a folded archicortical mantle, or 'ribbon' (Duvernoy, 1998).
evidence: Supported by citation to Duvernoy, 1998.

claim: Topological alignment accounts for much inter-individual variability in MRI-based manual subfield segmentations.
source: In previous work, this was shown to account for much inter-individual variability in MRI-based manual subfield segmentations (DeKraker et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to DeKraker et al., 2018.

claim: Representation of the hippocampus as a ribbon allows it to be factorized into surface area and thickness.
source: Additionally, representation as a ribbon allows the hippocampus to be factorized into surface area and thickness, which can be further subdivided for laminar analyses.
evidence: Stated as a direct consequence of the ribbon representation.

claim: The hippocampal archicortical ribbon is thin (0.5–2 mm).
source: Denoting the hippocampal archicortical ribbon is challenging because it is thin (0.5–2 mm), its folding pattern varies considerably between individuals (Chang et al., 2018; Ding and Van Hoesen, 2015), and this folding may even continue to change from early development through adulthood (Cai et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated as a measurement range.

claim: The hippocampal folding pattern varies considerably between individuals.
source: Denoting the hippocampal archicortical ribbon is challenging because it is thin (0.5–2 mm), its folding pattern varies considerably between individuals (Chang et al., 2018; Ding and Van Hoesen, 2015), and this folding may even continue to change from early development through adulthood (Cai et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chang et al., 2018 and Ding and Van Hoesen, 2015.

claim: Hippocampal folding may continue to change from early development through adulthood.
source: Denoting the hippocampal archicortical ribbon is challenging because it is thin (0.5–2 mm), its folding pattern varies considerably between individuals (Chang et al., 2018; Ding and Van Hoesen, 2015), and this folding may even continue to change from early development through adulthood (Cai et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Cai et al., 2019.

claim: HippUnfold uses a 'U-Net' deep learning architecture combined with topological constraints.
source: We present here a set of tools to overcome these challenges using a highly sensitive and generalizable 'U-Net' deep learning architecture (Isensee et al., 2021), combined with previous work that enforces topological constraints on hippocampal tissue (DeKraker et al., 2018).
evidence: Stated as the method used, with citations to Isensee et al., 2021 and DeKraker et al., 2018.

claim: A method was previously developed to computationally unfold the hippocampus along its geodesic anterior-posterior (AP) and proximal-distal (PD) axes.
source: In previous work (DeKraker et al., 2018), we developed a method to computationally unfold the hippocampus along its geodesic anterior-posterior (AP) and proximal-distal (PD, i.e. proximal to the neocortex, with the dentate gyrus [DG] being most distal) axes.
evidence: Supported by citation to DeKraker et al., 2018.

claim: All subfields are contiguous along the curvature of the hippocampal head (anterior) and tail (posterior).
source: We demonstrated for the first time several qualitative properties using in vivo MRI, such as the contiguity of all subfields along the curvature of the hippocampal head (anterior) and tail (posterior), previously described only in histology.
evidence: Stated as a finding from previous work (DeKraker et al., 2018).

claim: The stratum radiatum, lacunosum, and moleculare (SRLM) is a high-myelinated landmark that separates hippocampal folds along the inward 'curl' of the hippocampus.
source: This pioneering work relied heavily on detailed manual tissue segmentations including the high-myelinated stratum radiatum, lacunosum, and moleculare (SRLM), a commonly used landmark that separates hippocampal folds along the inward 'curl' of the hippocampus.
evidence: Stated as a characteristic of SRLM.

claim: Digitations along the AP axis of the hippocampus occur most prominently in the hippocampal head.
source: In this work we also considered curvature and digitations along the AP axis of the hippocampus, most prominently occurring in the hippocampal head (Duvernoy, 1998; Chang et al., 2018; Ding and Van Hoesen, 2015; DeKraker et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Duvernoy, 1998; Chang et al., 2018; Ding and Van Hoesen, 2015; DeKraker et al., 2018.

claim: Hippocampal morphological features are highly variable between individuals.
source: Each of these features are highly variable between individuals, making them difficult to capture using automated volumetric atlas-based methods and time-consuming to detect manually.
evidence: Stated as a challenge for existing methods.

claim: The current work automates detailed tissue segmentation required for hippocampal unfolding using a state-of-the-art 'U-Net' deep convolutional neural network.
source: The current work automates the detailed tissue segmentation required for hippocampal unfolding using a state-of-the-art 'U-Net' deep convolutional neural network (Isensee et al., 2021).
evidence: Stated as the method used, with citation to Isensee et al., 2021.

claim: U-Net architectures have been shown to be generalizable and sensitive to anatomical variations in many medical image processing tasks.
source: U-Net architectures have been shown to be generalizable and sensitive to anatomical variations in many medical image processing tasks (Du et al., 2020), making them ideal to overcome this challenge.
evidence: Supported by citation to Du et al., 2020.

claim: Estimating hippocampal subfield boundaries in MRI is challenging due to lower spatial resolution and lack of appropriate contrasts.
source: Estimating hippocampal subfield boundaries in MRI is challenging since their histological hallmarks are not directly available in MRI due to lower spatial resolution and lack of appropriate contrasts, which is an ongoing hurdle in neuroimaging (Wisse et al., 2017b; Yushkevich et al., 2015a).
evidence: Supported by citations to Wisse et al., 2017b and Yushkevich et al., 2015a.

claim: Post-mortem studies show that hippocampal subfields are topologically constrained according to their differentiation from a common flat cortical mantle.
source: However, post-mortem studies show that the subfields are topologically constrained according to their differentiation from a common flat cortical mantle (Duvernoy, 1998).
evidence: Supported by citation to Duvernoy, 1998.

claim: Surface-based subfield boundary definitions were obtained via manual segmentation of BigBrain 3D histology.
source: Here, we apply surface-based subfield boundary definitions obtained via manual segmentation of BigBrain 3D histology (Amunts et al., 2013) which was additionally supported by a data-driven parcellation (DeKraker et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Amunts et al., 2013 and DeKraker et al., 2020.

claim: HippUnfold combines novel U-Net tissue classification, previously developed hippocampal unfolding, and topologically constrained subfield labelling into a single pipeline.
source: Altogether, we combine novel U-Net tissue classification, previously developed hippocampal unfolding (DeKraker et al., 2018), and topologically constrained subfield labelling (DeKraker et al., 2020) together into a single pipeline which we refer to as 'HippUnfold' hereinafter.
evidence: Stated as the composition of the pipeline, with citations to DeKraker et al., 2018 and DeKraker et al., 2020.

claim: HippUnfold is designed to work with commonly employed sub-millimetric MRI acquisitions.
source: It is designed to work with commonly employed sub-millimetric MRI acquisitions, with possible extension to microscopic resolution.
evidence: Stated as a design feature.

claim: HippUnfold outputs include hippocampal tissue and subfield segmentations, geodesic Laplace coordinates, and inner, midthickness and outer hippocampal surfaces.
source: HippUnfold is presented here as a fully automated pipeline with outputs including hippocampal tissue and subfield segmentations, geodesic Laplace coordinates spanning over hippocampal GM voxels, and inner, midthickness and outer hippocampal surfaces.
evidence: Stated as the outputs of the pipeline.

claim: HippUnfold surfaces have corresponding vertices, providing an implicit topological registration between individuals.
source: These surfaces have corresponding vertices, providing an implicit topological registration between individuals.
evidence: Stated as a feature of the surfaces generated.

claim: A U-Net neural network architecture (nnUNet) is used to segment hippocampal grey matter (GM), the high-myelinated SRLM, and structures surrounding the hippocampus.
source: Second, a U-Net neural network architecture (nnUNet; Isensee et al., 2021) is used to segment hippocampal grey matter (GM), the high-myelinated stratum radiatum, lacunosum, and moleculare (SRLM), and structures surrounding the hippocampus.
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 1, with citation to Isensee et al., 2021.

claim: Laplace's equation is solved across the anterior-posterior (AP), proximal-distal (PD), and inner-outer (IO) extent of hippocampal GM to make up a geodesic coordinate framework.
source: Third, Laplace's equation is solved across the anterior-posterior (AP), proximal-distal (PD), and inner-outer (IO) extent of hippocampal GM, making up a geodesic coordinate framework.
evidence: Stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Scattered interpolants are used to determine equivalent coordinates between native Cartesian space and unfolded space.
source: Fourth, scattered interpolants are used to determine equivalent coordinates between native Cartesian space and unfolded space.
evidence: Stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Unfolded surfaces with template subfield labels are transformed to subjects' native folded hippocampal configurations.
source: Fifth, unfolded surfaces with template subfield labels (DeKraker et al., 2020) are transformed to subjects' native folded hippocampal configurations.
evidence: Stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1, with citation to DeKraker et al., 2020.

claim: Morphological features (e.g. thickness) are extracted using Connectome Workbench on folded native space surfaces.
source: Morphological features (e.g. thickness) are extracted using Connectome Workbench (Glasser et al., 2013) on these folded native space surfaces.
evidence: Stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1, with citation to Glasser et al., 2013.

claim: Volumetric subfields are generated by filling the voxels between inner and outer surfaces with the corresponding subfield labels.
source: Sixth, volumetric subfields are generated by filling the voxels between inner and outer surfaces with the corresponding subfield labels.
evidence: Stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: The nnUNet architecture was automatically configured as the 3D_fullres network, using 128 × 256 × 128 (0.3 × 0.3 × 0.3 mm3) hippocampal subregion images as training data.
source: This architecture was automatically configured as the 3D_fullres network, using the 128 × 256 × 128 (0.3 × 0.3 × 0.3 mm3) hippocampal subregion images as training data.
evidence: Stated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 caption.

claim: HippUnfold extracts morphological features and can be used to sample quantitative MRI data along a midthickness surface to minimize partial voluming with surrounding structures.
source: In addition to subfield segmentation, HippUnfold extracts morphological features and can be used to sample quantitative MRI data along a midthickness surface to minimize partial voluming with surrounding structures (see Materials and methods section 'HippUnfold detailed pipeline' for details).
evidence: Stated as a capability of the pipeline.

claim: Group averaging in HippUnfold takes place on a surface and does not break individual subjects' topologies.
source: Note that the group averaging takes place on a surface and so does not break individual subjects' topologies.
evidence: Stated as a property of the group averaging method.

claim: T1w/T2w ratio is a proxy measure for intracortical myelin.
source: Quantitative MRI features examined here include T1w/T2w ratio as a proxy measure for intracortical myelin (Ganzetti et al., 2014), mean diffusivity, and fractional anisotropy (Hernández et al., 2013; Sotiropoulos et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ganzetti et al., 2014.

claim: The dentate gyrus (DG) is represented as a distinct surface, reflecting its unique topology.
source: The dentate gyrus (DG) is represented as a distinct surface, reflecting its unique topology, and is mostly occluded in native space.
evidence: Stated in Figure 2 caption.

claim: Many morphological and quantitative MRI measures show clear distinctions across subfield boundaries.
source: Note that many morphological and quantitative MRI measures show clear distinctions across subfield boundaries.
evidence: Stated in Figure 2 caption and visible in the figure.

claim: Distortions were greatest in the tail of the hippocampus where its proximal-distal distance becomes quite narrow.
source: Distortions were greatest in the tail of the hippocampus where its proximal-distal distance becomes quite narrow.
evidence: Stated in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 caption.

claim: Clear differences in morphological and quantitative MRI features can be seen across the hippocampus, particularly across subfields as defined from a histologically derived unfolded reference atlas (3D BigBrain).
source: Clear differences in morphological and quantitative MRI features can be seen across the hippocampus, particularly across subfields as defined here from a histologically derived unfolded reference atlas (3D BigBrain) (DeKraker et al., 2020).
evidence: Stated as an observation from the results, with citation to DeKraker et al., 2020.

claim: Previous work examining differences in morphological and quantitative MRI features across hippocampal subfields showed features that differed between predefined subfields on average, but did not necessarily follow subfield contours.
source: These folded and unfolded representations of hippocampal characteristics are broadly in line with previous work examining differences in such morphological and quantitative MRI features across hippocampal subfields or along the hippocampal AP extent (e.g. Vos de Wael et al., 2018; Crombe et al., 2018). However, in previous work these features differed between predefined subfields on average, but did not necessarily follow subfield contours as seen here.
evidence: Stated as a comparison to previous work, with citations to Vos de Wael et al., 2018 and Crombe et al., 2018.

claim: Freesurfer v7.2.0 (FS7) and Automatic Segmentation of Hippocampal Subfields (ASHS) are among the most widely adopted automatic methods for labelling hippocampal subfields in MRI.
source: Several automatic methods for labelling hippocampal subfields in MRI exist, of which FS7 (Iglesias et al., 2015) and ASHS (Yushkevich et al., 2015b) are among the most widely adopted.
evidence: Stated as a fact about existing methods, with citations to Iglesias et al., 2015 and Yushkevich et al., 2015b.

claim: ASHS makes use of multi-atlas registration, wherein multiple gold standard manual hippocampal subfield segmentations are registered to a target sample.
source: Specifically, ASHS makes use of multi-atlas registration, wherein multiple gold standard manual hippocampal subfield segmentations are registered to a target sample.
evidence: Stated as a description of the ASHS method.

claim: The ASHS multi-atlas typically consists of roughly a dozen samples which are then fused together to generate a reliable yet oftentimes smooth or simplified final product.
source: Typically the multi-atlas consists of roughly a dozen samples which are then fused together to generate a reliable yet oftentimes smooth or simplified final product.
evidence: Stated as a characteristic of the ASHS method.

claim: Freesurfer uses a combination of voxel-wise classification and volumetric registration between a target hippocampus and a probabilistic reference atlas.
source: FS uses a combination of voxel-wise classification and, bijectively, volumetric registration between a target hippocampus and a probabilistic reference atlas, which is generated via combined in vivo MRI and 9.4T ex vivo hippocampal subfield segmentations (Iglesias et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated as a description of the FS method, with citation to Iglesias et al., 2015.

claim: When hippocampi take on different folding configurations, volumetric registrations can become ill-posed.
source: When hippocampi take on different folding configurations, such registrations can become ill-posed.
evidence: Stated as a limitation of volumetric registration methods.

claim: HippUnfold overcomes limitations of volumetric registration by using extensive training (n=590) with U-Net to capture detailed inter-individual differences in folding, and by using unfolding to ensure topologically constrained subfield labelling.
source: HippUnfold overcomes these limitations in two ways: with extensive training (in this case n=590), U-Net can capture detailed inter-individual differences in folding and, secondly, our unfolding technique ensures that subfield labelling is topologically constrained (DeKraker et al., 2021).
evidence: Stated as the advantages of HippUnfold, with citation to DeKraker et al., 2021.

claim: HippUnfold replicates the widely observed phenomenon of age-related decline in hippocampal subfield volumes, with similar effect sizes to FS and ASHS.
source: Quantitative comparison between methods shows an age-related decline in subfield volumes for all methods, with a relative sparing of CA3. Thus, HippUnfold replicates the widely observed phenomenon of age-related decline, with similar effect sizes to FS and ASHS (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated as a finding from the comparison, with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Bland-Altman plots show major differences in hippocampal subfield sizes between HippUnfold, FS, and ASHS methods.
source: Bland-Altman plots show major differences in hippocampal subfield sizes between methods, which most likely results from inclusion of the hippocampal tail in HippUnfold.
evidence: Stated as an observation from the Bland-Altman plots shown in Figure 3.

claim: The major differences in hippocampal subfield sizes between methods most likely result from inclusion of the hippocampal tail in HippUnfold.
source: Bland-Altman plots show major differences in hippocampal subfield sizes between methods, which most likely results from inclusion of the hippocampal tail in HippUnfold.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the Bland-Altman plot results.

claim: All three methods (HippUnfold, FS7, ASHS) showed a moderate correlation with age.
source: All three methods showed a moderate correlation with age, as expected based on previous literature.
evidence: Stated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 caption.

claim: There is a strong correlation between total hippocampal volumes obtained using HippUnfold and those obtained using FS7 or ASHS.
source: Volumetric comparison of each method to HippUnfold directly revealed that there is a strong correlation between total hippocampal volumes obtained using HippUnfold and those obtained using FS7 or ASHS.
evidence: Stated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 caption.

claim: HippUnfold and FS7 showed a moderate difference in overall hippocampal volume (FS7 being on average 540 mm3 larger).
source: HippUnfold and FS7 showed a moderate difference in overall volume (FS7 being on average 540 mm3 larger), whereas ASHS volumes were consistently smaller (by an average of 270 mm3).
evidence: Stated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 caption.

claim: ASHS volumes were consistently smaller than HippUnfold volumes (by an average of 270 mm3).
source: HippUnfold and FS7 showed a moderate difference in overall volume (FS7 being on average 540 mm3 larger), whereas ASHS volumes were consistently smaller (by an average of 270 mm3).
evidence: Stated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 caption.

claim: There was relatively low Dice overlap between subfield labels obtained using HippUnfold, FS7, and ASHS in native space.
source: At the subfield level, using an unfolded subfield atlas from the corresponding method, there was relatively low Dice overlap between labels obtained using these three different methods in native space, which is likely driven by the gross volume differences between methods (i.e. which tissues are included or excluded prior to unfolding) since subfield definitions are nearly identical after unfolding.
evidence: Stated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 caption.

claim: The low Dice overlap between subfield labels from different methods is likely driven by gross volume differences between methods (i.e. which tissues are included or excluded prior to unfolding) since subfield definitions are nearly identical after unfolding.
source: At the subfield level, using an unfolded subfield atlas from the corresponding method, there was relatively low Dice overlap between labels obtained using these three different methods in native space, which is likely driven by the gross volume differences between methods (i.e. which tissues are included or excluded prior to unfolding) since subfield definitions are nearly identical after unfolding.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 caption.

claim: Both ASHS and FS showed subfield discontinuities in unfolded space in at least some subjects.
source: Both ASHS and FS showed subfield discontinuities in unfolded space in at least some subjects, and FS even showed discontinuities in the group-averaged unfolded subfields.
evidence: Stated as an observation from the comparison.

claim: FS showed discontinuities in the group-averaged unfolded subfields.
source: Both ASHS and FS showed subfield discontinuities in unfolded space in at least some subjects, and FS even showed discontinuities in the group-averaged unfolded subfields.
evidence: Stated as an observation from the comparison.

claim: ASHS does not include an SRLM label.
source: ASHS does not include an SRLM label and the SRLM produced by FS was not consistently aligned with that used in unfolding.
evidence: Stated as a characteristic of ASHS.

claim: The SRLM produced by FS was not consistently aligned with that used in unfolding.
source: ASHS does not include an SRLM label and the SRLM produced by FS was not consistently aligned with that used in unfolding.
evidence: Stated as an observation about FS.

claim: Subfields in ASHS and FS sometimes erroneously crossed the SRLM, breaking topology.
source: Thus, subfields sometimes erroneously crossed the SRLM, breaking topology and explaining why discontinuities were sometimes observed in unfolded space.
evidence: Stated as an explanation for observed discontinuities.

claim: Ordering of subfield labels was not consistent in ASHS and FS.
source: Ordering of labels was also not consistent in ASHS and FS. For example, sometimes CA1 would border not only CA2 but also CA3, CA4, and/or DG.
evidence: Stated as an observation about ASHS and FS.

claim: Neither ASHS nor FS extends all subfields to the full anterior and posterior extent of the hippocampus.
source: Additionally, neither ASHS nor FS extends all subfields to the full anterior and posterior extent of the hippocampus.
evidence: Stated as a limitation of ASHS and FS.

claim: Both ASHS and FS simplify most of the anterior hippocampus as being CA1 and opt not to label subfields in the posterior hippocampus at all.
source: Instead, both methods simplify most of the anterior hippocampus as being CA1 and opt not to label subfields in the posterior hippocampus at all.
evidence: Stated as a characteristic of ASHS and FS.

claim: The simplifications in ASHS and FS are not in line with the anatomical ground truth shown in both classic and contemporary ex vivo histological studies.
source: These qualities are not in line with the anatomical ground truth shown in both classic and contemporary ex vivo histological studies (Duvernoy, 1998; Ding and Van Hoesen, 2015), which were indeed well captured by HippUnfold.
evidence: Stated as a comparison to histological ground truth, with citations to Duvernoy, 1998 and Ding and Van Hoesen, 2015.

claim: HippUnfold well captured the anatomical ground truth shown in both classic and contemporary ex vivo histological studies.
source: These qualities are not in line with the anatomical ground truth shown in both classic and contemporary ex vivo histological studies (Duvernoy, 1998; Ding and Van Hoesen, 2015), which were indeed well captured by HippUnfold.
evidence: Stated as a comparison to histological ground truth, with citations to Duvernoy, 1998 and Ding and Van Hoesen, 2015.

claim: FS over-labelled hippocampal tissue, which can be seen reaching laterally into the ventricles in the coronal view.
source: FS also over-labelled hippocampal tissue, which can be seen reaching laterally into the ventricles in the coronal view.
evidence: Stated as an observation about FS.

claim: Similar errors in FS have been documented in other recent work.
source: Similar errors have been documented for FS in other recent work (Wisse et al., 2014; Haast et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Wisse et al., 2014 and Haast et al., 2021.

claim: A set of 738 (left and right from 369 subjects) gold standard hippocampal tissue segmentations were generated from the HCP-YA dataset.
source: From the HCP-YA dataset, a set of 738 (left and right from 369 subjects) gold standard hippocampal tissue (i.e. hippocampal GM and surrounding structures) segmentations were generated according to the manual protocol defined in DeKraker et al., 2020.
evidence: Stated as the training data, with citation to DeKraker et al., 2020.

claim: Gold standard segmentations were generated by raters JD, MY, and BK using an incremental learning U-Net training regime.
source: Specifically, this was done by raters JD, MY, and BK using an incremental learning U-Net training regime described in the Materials and methods 'nnUNet training' section.
evidence: Stated as the method for generating training data.

claim: Automated tissue segmentation was performed using nnUNet, trained on 80% (n=590) of the gold standard segmentation data, with the remaining 20% (n=148) making up a test set.
source: Automated tissue segmentation was performed using nnUNet, a recent and highly generalizable implementation of a U-Net architecture (Isensee et al., 2021). This software was trained on 80% (n=590) of the gold standard segmentation data described above, with the remaining 20% (n=148) making up a test set.
evidence: Stated as the training/testing split, with citation to Isensee et al., 2021.

claim: Left and right hippocampi from the same participant were never split across training and testing sets due to their high symmetry.
source: Left and right hippocampi from the same participant were never split across training and testing sets due to their high symmetry.
evidence: Stated as a methodological decision.

claim: Within the training set, fivefold cross-validation was performed as implemented in the nnUNet code.
source: Within the training set, fivefold cross-validation was performed as implemented in the nnUNet code.
evidence: Stated as part of the training procedure.

claim: Training took place on an NVIDIA T4 Turing GPU over 72 hr.
source: Training took place on an NVIDIA T4 Turing GPU over 72 hr.
evidence: Stated as a detail of the training process.

claim: All default nnUNet data augmentation and hyperparameters were used.
source: All default nnUNet data augmentation and hyperparameters were used.
evidence: Stated as a methodological detail.

claim: Dice overlap depends heavily on the size of the label in question, being lower for smaller labels.
source: Dice overlap depends heavily on the size of the label in question, being lower for smaller labels.
evidence: Stated as a general property of Dice overlap.

claim: A Dice score of >0.7 is typically considered good.
source: Typically a score of >0.7 is considered good, and many fully manual protocols show dice scores of >0.8 for the larger subfields like CA1 or the subiculum, and 0.6–0.8 for smaller subfields like CA2 or CA3 (see Yushkevich et al., 2015a, for overview).
evidence: Stated as a benchmark, with citation to Yushkevich et al., 2015a.

claim: Many fully manual protocols show dice scores of >0.8 for the larger subfields like CA1 or the subiculum, and 0.6–0.8 for smaller subfields like CA2 or CA3.
source: Typically a score of >0.7 is considered good, and many fully manual protocols show dice scores of >0.8 for the larger subfields like CA1 or the subiculum, and 0.6–0.8 for smaller subfields like CA2 or CA3 (see Yushkevich et al., 2015a, for overview).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yushkevich et al., 2015a.

claim: Within the HCP-YA test set, HippUnfold performance was similar or better than most fully manual protocols for T1w and T2w data.
source: Within the HCP-YA test set, performance was similar or better than most fully manual protocols for T1w and T2w data.
evidence: Stated as a comparison to manual protocols.

claim: Performance on T1w images was only marginally poorer than T2w images.
source: Performance on T1w images was only marginally poorer than T2w images which typically better show the SRLM and are popular in manual subfield segmentation protocols (Yushkevich et al., 2015a).
evidence: Stated as a comparison between modalities, with citation to Yushkevich et al., 2015a.

claim: T2w images typically better show the SRLM and are popular in manual subfield segmentation protocols.
source: Performance on T1w images was only marginally poorer than T2w images which typically better show the SRLM and are popular in manual subfield segmentation protocols (Yushkevich et al., 2015a).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yushkevich et al., 2015a.

claim: Hippocampal morphometry, integrity, and subfields are often of interest in disease states where atrophy or other structural abnormalities are observed.
source: Hippocampal morphometry, integrity, and subfields are often of interest in disease states where atrophy or other structural abnormalities are observed (Thom, 2014; Haukvik et al., 2018; Steve et al., 2014; Carr et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Thom, 2014; Haukvik et al., 2018; Steve et al., 2014; Carr et al., 2017.

claim: The HCP-A dataset was examined because cases of severe atrophy were anticipated in some older subjects.
source: For this reason, we examined the HCP-A datasets in which we anticipated cases of severe atrophy would be present in some older subjects.
evidence: Stated as a rationale for examining the HCP-A dataset.

claim: Anisotropic T2w data is considered optimal for performing manual segmentation in most protocols.
source: Another common use-case for hippocampal subfield segmentation is on anisotropic T2w data which is considered optimal for performing manual segmentation in most protocols (Yushkevich et al., 2015a), but may impose challenges for our method due to the difference in resolution.
evidence: Supported by citation to Yushkevich et al., 2015a.

claim: A 37-year-old female right-handed patient was investigated for surgical treatment of temporal lobe epilepsy.
source: A 37-year-old female right-handed patient was investigated for surgical treatment of temporal lobe epilepsy, and clinical MR imaging at 1.5 T revealed a FLAIR hyper-intensity in the right hippocampus.
evidence: Stated as a case description.

claim: Clinical MR imaging at 1.5 T revealed a FLAIR hyper-intensity in the right hippocampus of the epilepsy patient.
source: A 37-year-old female right-handed patient was investigated for surgical treatment of temporal lobe epilepsy, and clinical MR imaging at 1.5 T revealed a FLAIR hyper-intensity in the right hippocampus.
evidence: Stated as a clinical finding.

claim: The epilepsy patient underwent a right anterior temporal lobectomy and has been seizure-free (Engel class 1) for 4 years.
source: The patient underwent a right anterior temporal lobectomy and has been seizure-free (Engel class 1) for 4 years.
evidence: Stated as a clinical outcome.

claim: Bilateral asymmetry is a strong indicator of epileptogenesis.
source: Bilateral asymmetry is a strong indicator of epileptogenesis, and so results are examined for both the left and right hippocampi.
evidence: Stated as a rationale for examining both hippocampi.

claim: The afflicted hippocampus in the epilepsy patient showed relative sparing of CA2, which is a common observation in hippocampal sclerosis.
source: Note that in addition to a loss in overall volume, the afflicted hippocampus showed relative sparing of CA2 which is a common observation in hippocampal sclerosis (Blümcke et al., 2013), as well as reduced digitations compared to the left hemisphere.
evidence: Stated as an observation, with citation to Blümcke et al., 2013.

claim: The afflicted hippocampus in the epilepsy patient showed reduced digitations compared to the left hemisphere.
source: Note that in addition to a loss in overall volume, the afflicted hippocampus showed relative sparing of CA2 which is a common observation in hippocampal sclerosis (Blümcke et al., 2013), as well as reduced digitations compared to the left hemisphere.
evidence: Stated as an observation.

claim: Examining additional patients in future work may reveal whether morphometry could be a clinical marker of epileptogenesis in patients with no remarkable clinical lesions.

claim: 188/1312 (14.3%) samples from the HCP-A T2w set were flagged for quality assurance.
source: This made up 34/2126 (1.6%) samples in the HCP-YA T2w set (including training and testing subsets), 188/1312 (14.3%) samples from the HCP-A T2w set, 37/1312 (2.8%) samples from the HCP-A T1w set, and 3/92 (3.3%) samples from the 7T-TSE set.

claim: 37/1312 (2.8%) samples from the HCP-A T1w set were flagged for quality assurance.

claim: The high number of flagged cases in HCP-A T2w was likely not due to the age of subjects since few of the HCP-A T1w were flagged as possible errors.
source: This was likely not due to the age of subjects since few of the HCP-A T1w were flagged as possible errors, but instead may have been due to T2w scan quality, which was observed to be poor in some subjects, causing poor definition of the outer hippocampal boundaries.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the flagging results.

claim: The high number of flagged cases in HCP-A T2w may have been due to T2w scan quality, which was observed to be poor in some subjects, causing poor definition of the outer hippocampal boundaries.
source: This was likely not due to the age of subjects since few of the HCP-A T1w were flagged as possible errors, but instead may have been due to T2w scan quality, which was observed to be poor in some subjects, causing poor definition of the outer hippocampal boundaries.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the flagging results.

claim: It is possible to synthesize or convert between MRI modalities, which could be used to alleviate the dependency on any single MR contrast.

claim: Within the generalization datasets examined, HippUnfold results were excellent.

claim: Fewer failures were observed in HippUnfold using T1w data compared to T2w data.
source: It is interesting to note that fewer failures were observed in HippUnfold using T1w data compared to T2w data (Figure 7), even though performance of nnUNet tissue classification were slightly higher with T2w images (Figure 5) and these are more common in hippocampal subfield imaging literature.
evidence: Stated as an observation, with references to Figures 5 and 7.

claim: Failed cases often had poor image quality, with subsequent issues like linear misregistration to the common CITI168 atlas or catastrophic nnUNet tissue classification failures.
source: Examining some failed cases, we see that these often had poor image quality, with subsequent issues like linear misregistration to the common CITI168 atlas or catastrophic nnUNet tissue classification failures.
evidence: Stated as an observation from examining failed cases.

claim: HippUnfold was designed to employ FAIR principles (findability, accessibility, interoperability, reusability).
source: We designed this pipeline to employ FAIR principles (findability, accessibility, interoperability, reusability) with support across a wide range of use-cases centred around sub-millimetric MRI.
evidence: Stated as a design goal.

claim: The default file input-output structure of the HippUnfold command-line interface was built in compliance with the Brain Imaging Data Standards (BIDS) Applications (BIDS-Apps) guidelines.
source: The default file input-output structure of the HippUnfold command-line interface was built in compliance with the Brain Imaging Data Standards (BIDS) (Gorgolewski et al., 2016) Applications (BIDS-Apps) guidelines (Gorgolewski et al., 2017), and easily findable amongst the list of available BIDS Apps [https://bids-apps.neuroimaging.io/apps/].
evidence: Stated as a design feature, with citations to Gorgolewski et al., 2016 and Gorgolewski et al., 2017.

claim: HippUnfold uses Snakebids, a tool designed to interface between BIDS datasets and Snakemake.
source: This is achieved via Snakebids, a tool designed to interface between BIDS datasets and Snakemake (Khan and Haast, 2021).
evidence: Stated as a tool used, with citation to Khan and Haast, 2021.

claim: All aspects of HippUnfold use Snakemake, a workflow management system based on Python which is reproducible, scalable, and seamlessly combines shell commands, Python code, and external dependencies in a human-readable workflow.
source: All aspects of HippUnfold use Snakemake (Mölder et al., 2021), a workflow management system based on Python which is reproducible, scalable, and seamlessly combines shell commands, Python code, and external dependencies in a human-readable workflow.
evidence: Stated as a tool used, with citation to Mölder et al., 2021.

claim: HippUnfold dependencies are containerized within the Singularity or Docker versions.
source: There is no need to install these dependencies, which are containerized within the Singularity or Docker versions of HippUnfold.
evidence: Stated as a feature of the software distribution.

claim: HippUnfold can be applied intelligently to any BIDS-complaint dataset containing a whole-brain T1w image or a T2w image (whole-brain or limited field of view) in a single line without having to specify further details.
source: Altogether, this means that in a single line this pipeline can be applied intelligently to any BIDS-complaint dataset containing a whole-brain T1w image or a T2w image (whole-brain or limited field of view) without having to specify further details.
evidence: Stated as a feature of the pipeline.

claim: Typical runtimes on a standard desktop are 30–60 min per subject.
source: Typical runtimes on a standard desktop are 30–60 min per subject, but this is further parallelized for faster processing when multiple subjects and added compute resources (or cloud computing) are available.
evidence: Stated as a performance characteristic.

claim: HippUnfold processing is further parallelized for faster processing when multiple subjects and added compute resources (or cloud computing) are available.
source: Typical runtimes on a standard desktop are 30–60 min per subject, but this is further parallelized for faster processing when multiple subjects and added compute resources (or cloud computing) are available.
evidence: Stated as a feature of the pipeline.

claim: Outputs of HippUnfold follow the standards for BIDS derivatives.
source: Outputs of HippUnfold follow the standards for BIDS derivatives, and include preprocessed input images, volumetric subfield segmentations, inner, midthickness, and outer hippocampal surfaces, vertex-wise morphometric measures of thickness, curvature, and gyrification, and a brief quality control (QC) report.
evidence: Stated as a feature of the outputs.

claim: All surface-based outputs are combined into a Connectome Workbench specification file for straightforward visualization analogous to HCP neocortical reconstructions.
source: All surface-based outputs are combined into a Connectome Workbench (Marcus et al., 2013) specification file for straightforward visualization analogous to HCP neocortical reconstructions.
evidence: Stated as a feature of the outputs, with citation to Marcus et al., 2013.

claim: One of the most powerful features of HippUnfold is its ability to provide topological alignment between subjects despite differences in folding (or digitation) structure.
source: One of the most powerful features of HippUnfold is its ability to provide topological alignment between subjects despite differences in folding (or digitation) structure.
evidence: Stated as a key feature of the method.

claim: Topological alignment is a critical element of mainstream neocortical analysis methods that, until now, has not been carried out systematically in the archicortex, or hippocampus.
source: This is a critical element of mainstream neocortical analysis methods that, until now, has not been carried out systematically in the archicortex, or hippocampus.
evidence: Stated as a contribution of the work.

claim: The power of topological alignment is evident when mapping morphological or quantitative features across the hippocampus in a large population.
source: The power of this form of topological alignment is evident when mapping morphological or quantitative features across the hippocampus in a large population, which we demonstrate in Figure 2.
evidence: Stated as a demonstration, with reference to Figure 2.

claim: Segmentation of subfields is a task that is conceptually simplified through unfolding of the hippocampus to provide intrinsic anatomical axes.
source: Segmentation of subfields is a task that is conceptually simplified through unfolding of the hippocampus to provide intrinsic anatomical axes.
evidence: Stated as a conceptual advantage of unfolding.

claim: The PD axis, which follows along the SLM in a coronal slice, is a landmark relied upon in many manual segmentation protocols for the hippocampal subfields.
source: The axis we define as PD, which follows along the SLM in a coronal slice, is also a landmark relied upon in many manual segmentation protocols for the hippocampal subfields, including a histologically validated protocol that defines subfield boundaries by the proportional distance along the SLM (Steve et al., 2017).
evidence: Stated as a connection to existing protocols, with citation to Steve et al., 2017.

claim: The head and tail are areas where manual segmentation heuristics have conventionally been very difficult to apply, since the slice angulation optimal for the body is not optimal for the curved head and tail.
source: The head and tail are areas where these heuristics have conventionally been very difficult to apply, since the slice angulation optimal for the body is not optimal for the curved head and tail, and work using multiplanar reformatting provides one alternative for curved regions of the hippocampus (Gross et al., 2020).
evidence: Stated as a challenge in manual segmentation, with citation to Gross et al., 2020.

claim: The unfolding approach is conceptually analogous to multiplanar reformatting approaches.
source: Our unfolding approach is conceptually analogous to these approaches, however, the added strength of our approach is that we apply the same conceptual rule (proportional distance along the SLM) while considering the entire 3D structure of the hippocampus.
evidence: Stated as a comparison to existing approaches.

claim: The added strength of the unfolding approach is that it applies the same conceptual rule (proportional distance along the SLM) while considering the entire 3D structure of the hippocampus.
source: Our unfolding approach is conceptually analogous to these approaches, however, the added strength of our approach is that we apply the same conceptual rule (proportional distance along the SLM) while considering the entire 3D structure of the hippocampus.
evidence: Stated as an advantage of the method.

claim: HippUnfold did not consistently show clear digitation in the hippocampal head, body, and tail which was sometimes seen in manual segmentation in the training set and in other work.
source: One important limitation of our method is that HippUnfold did not consistently show clear digitation in the hippocampal head, body, and tail which was sometimes seen in manual segmentation in the training set and in other work (see Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated as a limitation, with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The lack of clear digitation in HippUnfold reflects a lack of detail compared to histological ground truth materials.
source: This reflects a lack of detail compared to histological ground truth materials, and affects downstream processing.
evidence: Stated as an interpretation of the limitation.

claim: An overly smoothed hippocampal surface will appear thicker and have a smaller surface area compared to one that captures the full extent of digitations.
source: That is, an overly smoothed hippocampal surface will appear thicker and have a smaller surface area compared to one that captures the full extent of digitations.
evidence: Stated as a consequence of the smoothing.

claim: A smaller surface area results in each subfield boundary being proportionally shifted.
source: This smaller surface area also results in each subfield boundary being proportionally shifted.
evidence: Stated as a consequence of the smaller surface area.

claim: Future work could improve the HippUnfold pipeline by training and testing with higher-resolution data where digitations can more clearly be distinguished both in labelmaps and in the underlying images.
source: Future work could improve this pipeline by training and testing with higher-resolution data where digitations can more clearly be distinguished both in labelmaps and in the underlying images.
evidence: Stated as a suggestion for future work.

claim: A single unfolded subfield atlas based on 3D BigBrain ground truth histology was employed within HippUnfold for all subjects.
source: A single unfolded subfield atlas based on 3D BigBrain ground truth histology (DeKraker et al., 2020) was employed within HippUnfold for all subjects here.
evidence: Stated as a methodological choice, with citation to DeKraker et al., 2020.

claim: Alternative unfolded subfield atlases can be used in HippUnfold.
source: As illustrated in Figure 4, alternative unfolded subfield atlases can be used as well.
evidence: Stated as a feature of the pipeline, with reference to Figure 4.

claim: Previous work demonstrated reduced inter-individual variability of subfield boundaries in unfolded space.
source: Though previous work demonstrated reduced inter-individual variability of subfield boundaries in unfolded space (DeKraker et al., 2018), the extent to which subfield boundaries vary after unfolding is not yet known.
evidence: Supported by citation to DeKraker et al., 2018.

claim: The extent to which subfield boundaries vary after unfolding is not yet known.
source: Though previous work demonstrated reduced inter-individual variability of subfield boundaries in unfolded space (DeKraker et al., 2018), the extent to which subfield boundaries vary after unfolding is not yet known.
evidence: Stated as an open question.

source: In the neocortex, this issue is also present but partially mitigated with surface-based registration of available features like intracortical myelin, sulcal patterns, or thickness (e.g. Glasser et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Glasser et al., 2016.

claim: Information like intracortical myelin, sulcal patterns, or thickness could be used in the unfolded hippocampus to further refine subject-specific subfield delineation.
source: Such information could also be used in the unfolded hippocampus to further refine subject-specific subfield delineation, but would require histological ground truth data from multiple subjects to evaluate, ideally in 3D to avoid common out-of-plane sampling issues (DeKraker et al., 2021).
evidence: Stated as a possibility for future work, with citation to DeKraker et al., 2021.

claim: Refining subject-specific subfield delineation would require histological ground truth data from multiple subjects to evaluate, ideally in 3D to avoid common out-of-plane sampling issues.
source: Such information could also be used in the unfolded hippocampus to further refine subject-specific subfield delineation, but would require histological ground truth data from multiple subjects to evaluate, ideally in 3D to avoid common out-of-plane sampling issues (DeKraker et al., 2021).
evidence: Stated as a requirement for future work, with citation to DeKraker et al., 2021.

claim: This level of precision is likely beyond current typical MRI resolution levels, but should be investigated in future work aiming to combine in vivo and ex vivo or other more specialized imaging.
source: This level of precision is likely beyond current typical MRI resolution levels, but should be investigated in future work aiming to combine in vivo and ex vivo or other more specialized imaging.
evidence: Stated as a limitation and suggestion for future work.

claim: The current work has applications beyond subfield imaging, enabling new investigations of the hippocampus on a columnar and laminar scale.
source: The current work has applications beyond subfield imaging, enabling new investigations of the hippocampus on a columnar and laminar scale.
evidence: Stated as a broader application of the work.

claim: Rather than employing subfield ROI-based analyses, statistics can be performed on a per-vertex basis for vertices generated at different depths.
source: For example, rather than employing subfield ROI-based analyses, statistics can be performed on a per-vertex basis for vertices generated at different depths.
evidence: Stated as a possible application.

claim: Per-vertex analysis is in line with state-of-the-art neocortical analysis methods.
source: This is in line with state-of-the-art neocortical analysis methods (Van Essen et al., 2000), and opens up the possibility of more precise localization of hippocampal properties.

claim: The methods used in HippUnfold are not necessarily restricted to MRI, as the same surface-based unfolding has been used in combination with manual segmentation to characterize the hippocampus in 3D BigBrain histology.

evidence: Stated as a broader application, with citation to DeKraker et al., 2020.

claim: HippUnfold respects the different internal hippocampal folding configurations seen between individuals.
source: Altogether, we show that the BIDS App 'HippUnfold' that we have developed in this work (i) respects the different internal hippocampal folding configurations seen between individuals, (ii) can be applied flexibly to T1w or T2w data, sub-millimetric isotropic or thick-slice anisotropic data, and (iii) compares favourably to other popular methods including manual segmentation, ASHS and FS7.
evidence: Stated as a summary of the work.

claim: HippUnfold can be applied flexibly to T1w or T2w data, sub-millimetric isotropic or thick-slice anisotropic data.
source: Altogether, we show that the BIDS App 'HippUnfold' that we have developed in this work (i) respects the different internal hippocampal folding configurations seen between individuals, (ii) can be applied flexibly to T1w or T2w data, sub-millimetric isotropic or thick-slice anisotropic data, and (iii) compares favourably to other popular methods including manual segmentation, ASHS and FS7.
evidence: Stated as a summary of the work.

claim: HippUnfold compares favourably to other popular methods including manual segmentation, ASHS and FS7.
source: Altogether, we show that the BIDS App 'HippUnfold' that we have developed in this work (i) respects the different internal hippocampal folding configurations seen between individuals, (ii) can be applied flexibly to T1w or T2w data, sub-millimetric isotropic or thick-slice anisotropic data, and (iii) compares favourably to other popular methods including manual segmentation, ASHS and FS7.
evidence: Stated as a summary of the work.

claim: HippUnfold will open up many avenues for future work including examination of variability in hippocampal morphology which may show developmental trajectories or be linked to disease.
source: We believe this tool will open up many avenues for future work including examination of variability in hippocampal morphology which may show developmental trajectories or be linked to disease, or the examination of hippocampal properties perpendicular or tangential to its laminar organization with diffusion-weighted imaging.

claim: HippUnfold will enable examination of hippocampal properties perpendicular or tangential to its laminar organization with diffusion-weighted imaging.
source: We believe this tool will open up many avenues for future work including examination of variability in hippocampal morphology which may show developmental trajectories or be linked to disease, or the examination of hippocampal properties perpendicular or tangential to its laminar organization with diffusion-weighted imaging.
evidence: Stated as a belief about future applications.

claim: The methods described in HippUnfold stand to improve existing techniques by providing greater anatomical detail and, critically, greater precision through topological alignment across individuals who vary in anatomical structure.
source: Finally, it is worth noting that the methods described here stand to improve existing techniques by providing greater anatomical detail and, critically, greater precision through topological alignment across individuals who vary in anatomical structure.
evidence: Stated as a summary of the contribution.

claim: HippUnfold was designed and trained with the HCP 1200 young adult subject data release (HCP-YA).
source: HippUnfold was designed and trained with the HCP 1200 young adult subject data release (HCP-YA) (Van Essen et al., 2013), and additionally tested on the HCP-A dataset (Bookheimer et al., 2019), and anisotropic (or thick-slice) 7T data (7T-TSE) from Berron et al., 2017, which is considered optimal by many hippocampal subfield researchers (Yushkevich et al., 2015a).
evidence: Stated as the training data, with citations to Van Essen et al., 2013, Bookheimer et al., 2019, Berron et al., 2017, and Yushkevich et al., 2015a.

claim: HippUnfold was additionally tested on the HCP-A dataset.
source: HippUnfold was designed and trained with the HCP 1200 young adult subject data release (HCP-YA) (Van Essen et al., 2013), and additionally tested on the HCP-A dataset (Bookheimer et al., 2019), and anisotropic (or thick-slice) 7T data (7T-TSE) from Berron et al., 2017, which is considered optimal by many hippocampal subfield researchers (Yushkevich et al., 2015a).
evidence: Stated as the testing data, with citation to Bookheimer et al., 2019.

claim: HippUnfold was additionally tested on anisotropic (or thick-slice) 7T data (7T-TSE) from Berron et al., 2017.
source: HippUnfold was designed and trained with the HCP 1200 young adult subject data release (HCP-YA) (Van Essen et al., 2013), and additionally tested on the HCP-A dataset (Bookheimer et al., 2019), and anisotropic (or thick-slice) 7T data (7T-TSE) from Berron et al., 2017, which is considered optimal by many hippocampal subfield researchers (Yushkevich et al., 2015a).
evidence: Stated as the testing data, with citations to Berron et al., 2017 and Yushkevich et al., 2015a.

claim: Anisotropic (or thick-slice) 7T data is considered optimal by many hippocampal subfield researchers.
source: HippUnfold was designed and trained with the HCP 1200 young adult subject data release (HCP-YA) (Van Essen et al., 2013), and additionally tested on the HCP-A dataset (Bookheimer et al., 2019), and anisotropic (or thick-slice) 7T data (7T-TSE) from Berron et al., 2017, which is considered optimal by many hippocampal subfield researchers (Yushkevich et al., 2015a).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yushkevich et al., 2015a.

claim: U-Nets perform classification of each input image voxel, and are not constrained by smooth displacements used in deformable atlas registration.
source: U-Nets perform classification of each input image voxel, and it is not constrained by smooth displacements used in deformable atlas registration.
evidence: Stated as a characteristic of U-Nets.

claim: Smooth deformable registration can be ill-posed for an atlas with a different hippocampal folding configuration than the target.
source: This is important because smooth deformable registration can be ill-posed for an atlas with a different hippocampal folding configuration than the target.
evidence: Stated as a limitation of deformable registration.

claim: When trying to register a hippocampus with two anterior digitations to one with four anterior digitations, topological breaks may be seen which leads to loss of detail and disproportionate stretching or compression of some subfields.
source: For example, when trying to register a hippocampus with two anterior digitations to one with four anterior digitations, topological breaks may be seen which leads to loss of detail and disproportionate stretching or compression of some subfields, an issue that is discussed in DeKraker et al., 2021.
evidence: Stated as an example of the problem, with citation to DeKraker et al., 2021.

claim: A U-Net classifies voxels individually based on a combination of local low-level and global high-level image features with no explicit smoothness constraints.
source: Instead, a U-Net classifies voxels individually based on a combination of local low-level and global high-level image features with no explicit smoothness constraints.
evidence: Stated as a characteristic of U-Nets.

claim: Gold standard training and test comparison segmentations were generated in a semi-automated but heavily supervised manner using a U-Net implementation (NiftyNet).
source: In the current work, gold standard training and test comparison segmentations were generated in a semi-automated but heavily supervised manner: a U-Net implementation (NiftyNet; Gibson et al., 2018, which is no longer maintained) was trained on existing data from DeKraker et al., 2018.
evidence: Stated as the method for generating training data, with citations to Gibson et al., 2018 and DeKraker et al., 2018.

claim: The process of inspection and manual correction was always performed according to the protocol outlined in DeKraker et al., 2018, to avoid systematic drift in rater performance.
source: The process of inspection and manual correction was always performed according to the protocol outlined in DeKraker et al., 2018, to avoid systematic drift in rater performance.
evidence: Stated as a quality control measure, with citation to DeKraker et al., 2018.

claim: Incremental learning was applied in four iterations until a larger set of high quality, manually inspected and corrected segmentations (738 samples from 369 subjects) was achieved.
source: This process is typically referred to as incremental learning, and was applied in four iterations until a larger set of high quality, manually inspected and corrected segmentations (738 samples from 369 subjects) was achieved.
evidence: Stated as the training procedure.

claim: nnUNet was built to include many state-of-the art deep learning techniques including sensible hyperparameter selection, built-in fivefold cross-validation, and other features that have been shown to perform well and minimize possible sources of bias in medical imaging.
source: nnUNet was built to include many state-of-the art deep learning techniques including sensible hyperparameter selection, built-in fivefold cross-validation, and other features that have been shown to perform well and minimize possible sources of bias in medical imaging.
evidence: Stated as a characteristic of nnUNet.

claim: Training was repeated using the same labelmaps but different underlying images for T1w, T2w, and DWI images.
source: Training was repeated using the same labelmaps but different underlying images for T1w, T2w, and DWI images.
evidence: Stated as the training procedure.

claim: For each modality (T1w, T2w, DWI), training took place on an NVIDIA T4 Turing GPU over 72 hr.
source: For each of these modalities, training took place on an NVIDIA T4 Turing GPU over 72 hr.
evidence: Stated as a detail of the training process.

claim: A Laplace field varying from 0 to 1 is generated across hippocampal GM, with 0 being at its anterior boundary with the HATA and 1 being at its posterior boundary with the IndGris (AP).
source: A Laplace field varying from 0 to 1 is generated across hippocampal GM, with 0 being at its anterior boundary with the HATA and 1 being at its posterior boundary with the IndGris (AP).
evidence: Stated as a step in the unfolding process.

claim: The Laplace field provides a scaled, smooth, geodesic way to index points along the AP axis.
source: This provides a scaled, smooth, geodesic way to index points along this axis.
evidence: Stated as a property of the Laplace field.

claim: Another Laplace field is generated across the PD axis of the hippocampus (MTLc to DG), and together these two fields provide a coordinate system spanning hippocampus GM along two dimensions.
source: Another Laplace field is generated across the PD axis of the hippocampus (MTLc to DG), and together these two fields provide a coordinate system spanning hippocampus GM along two dimensions, which we plot as a flat rectangle (with a 2:1 aspect ratio to reflect the fact that the hippocampus is longer than it is wide).
evidence: Stated as a step in the unfolding process.

claim: A third Laplace field is generated across the thickness of hippocampal GM (SRLM to outer boundary, or inner to outer, or IO).
source: A third field is generated across the thickness of hippocampal GM (SRLM to outer boundary, or inner to outer, or IO).
evidence: Stated as a step in the unfolding process.

claim: By default, the IO Laplace field is replaced by an equivolumetric model, which helps account for the effects of curvature on laminar features.
source: By default, the IO Laplace field is replaced by an equivolumetric model (Waehnert et al., 2014; Huntenburg et al., 2018), which helps account for the effects of curvature on laminar features (though this replacement can optionally be disabled).
evidence: Stated as a methodological choice, with citations to Waehnert et al., 2014 and Huntenburg et al., 2018.

claim: Displacement fields are computed for transforming each voxel from native space to the 'unfolded' space spanned by the AP, PD, and IO fields, and vice versa.
source: We then compute displacement fields for transforming each voxel from native space to the 'unfolded' space spanned by these three (AP, PD, and IO) fields, and vice versa.
evidence: Stated as a step in the unfolding process.

claim: Piecewise linear interpolation (griddata from SciPy) is performed to go from each unfolded coordinate (AP, PD, IO) back to Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z).
source: We performed piecewise linear interpolation (griddata from SciPy; Virtanen et al., 2020) to go from each unfolded coordinate (AP, PD, IO) to back to Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z).
evidence: Stated as a step in the unfolding process, with citation to Virtanen et al., 2020.

claim: Laplace gradients are scaled to make up a standard rectangular prism with a size of 256 × 128 × 16 voxels (dimensions corresponding to AP, PD, and IO, respectively), at a voxel size of 0.15625 mm3 isotropic.
source: Rather than map Cartesian coordinates to Laplace coordinates ranging from 0 to 1 (as in previous work; DeKraker et al., 2018), we scale these gradients to make up a standard rectangular prism with a size of 256 × 128 × 16 voxels (dimensions corresponding to AP, PD, and IO, respectively), at a voxel size of 0.15625 mm3 isotropic.
